priceSnapshot.note: Down 3.25 percent on the rolling 24h open of 80,478.3 and DOWN 1,749.7 points - 2.20 percent - against the 79,609.9 morning mark. This is the largest session-over-session move in the log. The cause is dateable to the minute: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivered his Jackson Hole keynote and said inflation is running too high and that the summer's softer prints do not tell him underlying trends have improved. DXY jumped 0.56 percent to 99.712 and the US 10-year added 5.6 basis points to 4.728 percent, and BTC broke three 1H EMAs in two hours: the 15:00Z bar closed 78,329.9 and the 16:00Z bar closed 77,785.9 after printing 76,888.0. Price has since recovered 972.2 points off that low. The UTC day now spans 81,499.9 to 76,888.0, a 4,611.9-point range worth 2.02 daily ATRs - a genuine outside-reversal day, not a drift.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below $77,480.0 AND a failure to reclaim it on either of the next two hourly bars. Spot is 380.2 points above it, 0.59 hourly ATRs at the current 648.46 - the top of the 0.4-to-0.6 band every gate in this log has been written in. The level is structural rather than round: it sits just under the 77,500.0 liquidation rung that absorbed 1,928,262 USD across 201 fills on the way down, so a settled close beneath it means that shelf failed to hold on the retest. The four-bar reclaim amendment proposed on 27 August midday does not apply - it was written for a contracting, quiet tape, and hourly ATR has EXPANDED 40.0 percent this session from 463.06 to 648.46.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE above $78,160.0. Spot is 299.8 points below it, 0.46 hourly ATRs - inside the band. The level clears the 78,129.5 high of the in-progress 17:00Z bar by 30.5 points and reclaims the 78,000.0 liquidation shelf where 2,271,505 USD was cleared during the break. A settled close above it says the Warsh breakdown failed to hold its own ledge and the flush was positioning rather than repricing; below it, every rally is a lower high.

liquidation.note: 4,339,259 USD across 199 fills at ZERO percent short-side - every single fill in the bucket is a long being taken out. It is the largest cluster in the 23.4-hour window by 52 percent and sits 860.2 points below spot, 1.33 hourly ATRs. Marked as the magnet. One caveat that matters more than usual today: this records forced flow that ALREADY happened as price cut through the level on the 16:00Z bar, not resting orders sitting there now. By the lesson this desk logged only this morning - a one-sided cluster holds on the first visit and turns fragile on the second, once the forced flow beneath it is spent - the shelf is now the weak kind, not the strong kind.

2,857,848 USD across 144 fills at 2.1 percent short-side, so effectively another pure long flush. It is the second-heaviest bucket in the window and the first real obstacle between spot and the 77,000.0 magnet.

calibration.rollingRecord: Seventeen sessions logged. Morning's reduce gate is the first in this window to fire TWICE and be graded on the second trigger, and it is the first gate whose confirmation was worth more than 1,400 points. Running tally on the 0.4-to-0.6 ATR band: three clean confirmations, two whipsaws, and now one gate that whipsawed on trigger one and confirmed decisively on trigger two - which argues the band is fine and that a single trigger was never meant to be the whole signal.
calibration.note: Morning's REDUCE gate at a settled 1H close below 79,400.0 fired TWICE. Trigger one came at the 13:00Z close of 79,318.2, and it did NOT confirm - the very next bar, 14:00Z, closed 79,544.3, a clean 144.3 points back above the line, which by the letter of the two-bar reclaim rule voids it and would have been the window's third whipsaw. Trigger two came at the 15:00Z close of 78,329.9, 1,070.1 points through the line, and it CONFIRMED immediately: the 16:00Z bar closed 77,785.9, further below. Against the current 77,860.2, acting on trigger one would have sold at 79,318.2 and be 1,458.0 points better off; acting on trigger two, 469.7 points better off. acting_helped is TRUE on both readings. Morning's ADD gate at 79,880.0 did NOT fire and was never close - the highest settled close after publication was 79,544.3 on the 14:00Z bar, 335.7 points short, and the highest print was 79,839.3, still 40.7 points under the line. The close-only rule did no harm here. The transferable finding is about the whipsaw count itself: two of the three 'whipsaws' now logged were followed within two hours by a second trigger in the same direction that ran hard. A voided trigger is not evidence the level was wrong; it is evidence the first probe was early. Endday should grade gates on the SEQUENCE of triggers rather than only the first.
